surface.reason: 2xx response is a raw binary zip archive, not a JSON-schema-describable value -- rpc_endpoint (design §7) has no way to express a bytes-typed return with no response schema.

spec.description:
Retrieve a processed data export. Unlike every other Account Data endpoint, the response is not the standard `{error, result}` JSON envelope -- it is the raw export file itself.

**API Key Permissions Required:** `Data - Export data`

response.title: RetrieveExportResult
response.description: Metadata about the binary zip archive body, captured in place of the raw bytes (see `notes`). The real, hand-written `retrieve_export` method returns `bytes`, not this shape -- this schema documents the spec/example convention only.

content_type.description: The real response's `Content-Type` header. Observed live as `application/zip`, not the `application/octet-stream` upstream's OpenAPI declares -- see `notes`.

content_length.description: Size of the binary body in bytes.

magic_bytes.description: First 4 bytes of the body, hex-encoded, confirming the ZIP local-file-header signature (`504b0304` = `PK\x03\x04`).

note.description: Free-text explanation of why this is metadata rather than the raw archive.

notes: This endpoint's real 200 response is a binary zip archive (`Content-Type: application/zip` observed live -- upstream's OpenAPI declares `application/octet-stream`, which doesn't match), not the standard `{error, result}` JSON envelope every other Account Data endpoint uses. There is nothing to `extract`, so no `envelope` field is declared. The spec format/tooling (`docs/spec/spec.md`, `typed-dev spec test`) has no representation for a non-JSON response body -- `spec test` hard-requires an `application/json` media type to validate against -- so, rather than leaving this endpoint permanently failing that gate or inventing a fake JSON envelope the venue never sends, the response schema and captured example both describe metadata *about* the binary body (content-type, length, a magic-bytes signature check) instead of the bytes themselves. The real, hand-written core method (`surface.kind == 'handwritten'`, codegen-mechanization migration) still returns the raw bytes/stream to its caller; this is a spec/tooling-representation choice, not a claim about what the venue or the real core returns. Errors, if any, would surface as an HTTP-level failure or a non-binary body rather than the usual `error` array; not modeled here since this pass keeps 2xx responses only.
This is a documented toolchain gap (docs/spec/spec.md has no binary-response vocabulary), not a spec authored around a failing check.

Migrated off the legacy openapi/parameters/requestBody shape (codegen-mechanization, design §7) but kept `surface: handwritten`: the real return type (`bytes`) cannot be expressed by rpc_endpoint's schema-derived response_type, so this leaf stays a real, hand-written module (`Generator.skip_endpoint`'s default) rather than being regenerated.
